cohort: 329 pregnant women over a 2-year period who were > 37 weeks of gestational age and had a Bishop score < 5 prior to beginning labor induction
finding: Increasing BMI was significantly associated with longer time to delivery, a greater number of misoprostol doses required, longer duration of oxytocin administration, and an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Higher BMI was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
